newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat and Netanyahu to meet to clinch Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Arafat and Netanyahu to meet to clinch Hebron deal.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will meet on Tuesday to try to clinch a deal on a long-delayed handover of the West Bank town of Hebron to PLO-rule before Christmas.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu and President Arafat will meet on Tuesday at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT) at Erez to finalise an agreement on Hebron," said Arafat aide Nabil Abu Rdainah.
Israel and the PLO have accused each other of foot-dragging in more than three months of talks on Hebron, which was due to have been handed over to the Palestinians months ago.
Any deal on the West Bank city is likely to breathe new life into an Arab-Israeli peace process on the brink of collapse.
U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who shuttled between Israel, the Gaza Strip and Egypt in an effort to broker a deal, was to join the meeting on Tuesday, Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani said.
Israeli officials were not available for comment. But Netanyahu, when asked on Monday evening what was holding up an agreement, told reporters with a smile: "We are working it out, don't worry."
Abu Rdainah said the summit, to be held at the Erez crossing between Israel and the Gaza Strip, was a step towards an accord.
"Some issues were left to be finalised by the two leaders," he said.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators joined by Ross continued their talks early on Tuesday to create a draft agreement, said a PLO official who did not want to be identified.
The official said if the outstanding issues were resolved, a deal would be announced by the two leaders and the Israeli troop pullback from 80 percent of the city would begin within hours.

Netanyahu, who came to power in June vowing to take a tough line on Israeli security, has demanded protection for 400 Jewish militants in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs, a longtime flashpoint of violence between Arabs and Jews.

Earlier on Monday, PLO officials said Israel had dropped its insistence on having the right of hot pursuit of Palestinian suspects into PLO-held areas, accepting instead existing language in the Hebron handover agreement signed in 1995.
